title: Elodie and the Escarpment
premise: Zephyrine Ravensworth, a disgraced mountain guide with a blackened name and a compass that belonged to her missing mother, agrees to guide a dying prospector named Callum Voss over the Kestrel Escarpment in exchange for a hand-drawn map to the Meridian, a salvage wreck sunk in a lawless fjord. When Voss dies on the ridge, Zephyrine inherits both the map and his promise: deliver it to his estranged daughter, Wren, before the salvage fleet — led by the magistrate who ruined Zephyrine's career — reaches the wreck by the sixth tide. Guiding Wren through collapsing passes, rival salvagers, and her own guilt, Zephyrine discovers the wreck holds proof of the magistrate's forged survey that destroyed her mother's reputation years ago. In the climax at the sixth tide, they beat the fleet to the Meridian, recover the ledger proving the forgery, and expose the magistrate publicly; Zephyrine reclaims her name, Wren claims her inheritance, and both walk free of debts neither could pay alone.
about_author: Freya Eriksen is the pen name of a former alpine rescue volunteer who now writes adventure fiction from a cabin above the treeline. Her novels are known for brutal mountain settings, morally tangled inheritances, and heroines who owe more than they own.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Name
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Blacklisted and broke in the port town of Greyhollow, Zephyrine takes one last guiding contract: carry the coughing prospector Callum Voss over the Kestrel Escarpment. He offers triple pay and a secret. The beat is weary pragmatism masking old grief as she straps on her mother's compass.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Mid-ascent, Voss's lungs fail. Dying, he trades her a grease-stained map to the wrecked Meridian for a sworn promise: bring it to his daughter Wren before the dry season's sixth tide. The beat is reluctant oath-taking, the weight of a stranger's dying wish settling on her shoulders.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Hates Guides
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren Voss, a dock mechanic who blames guides for her father's absences, refuses to believe the news until Zephyrine produces the map in his handwriting. She demands to come along. The beat is flint-spark hostility between two women bound by a dead man's paper.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Descending toward the fjord, they learn the salvage fleet has already sailed under Magistrate Corvane Hale — the man whose forged survey ended Zephyrine's mother's career. They have six tides. The beat is cold dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Collapsing Pass
chapters.summary: POV Wren. A rockslide traps them in a defile; Wren freezes, and Zephyrine talks her through the climb down, revealing fragments of her mother's disgrace. Trust cracks open. The beat is fear transmuted into fragile, earned respect.

chapters.title: Smugglers' Toll
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. A river gang offers passage but demands the map as toll. Zephyrine bargains with a forged copy while Wren quietly steals back the original — justice outside the law, learned fast. The beat is exhilaration shadowed by the question of what they're becoming.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Sheltering in an abandoned watchtower, they decode the map's margins: Voss wasn't after treasure but a ledger hidden aboard the Meridian — proof of Hale's forged survey. Wren realizes her father died chasing her family's honor. The beat is grief reframed as purpose.

chapters.title: The Fleet at Anchor
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. From a cliff they watch Hale's flagship anchor off the wreck site, tide four spent. A storm front will buy them hours but kill anyone caught on the water. The beat is desperate calculation — the plan that follows should be impossible.

chapters.title: The Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Racing the storm, they dive the Meridian at slack water, seize the ledger as Hale's divers close in, and escape through the wreck's flooded hold as the sixth tide turns. Confrontation on the rocks: Hale's men versus two women with nothing left to lose. The beat is white-knuckle climax.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine then Wren. The ledger goes public; Hale falls, and Zephyrine's mother's name is cleared posthumously. Wren claims her father's estate; Zephyrine's blacklist dissolves. On the escarpment's edge they part — or don't quite. The beat is quiet, hard-won peace and an open horizon.
